title: Annotation chip system and scaling rules for dashboard overlays
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Design a reusable annotation chip component family for use across dashboards, rollout rails, and cost views. Deliver a Figma library with responsive scaling rules, token mappings, and an accessibility contrast matrix so engineering can ship a consistent, high-contrast component set that supports rollouts and inline state labels.
acceptance_criteria: Figma library includes primary, subtle, and inverse chip variants with tokens exposed
Scaling rules defined for 3 size breakpoints (compact, regular, spacious) and documented examples across 4 dashboard densities
Contrast matrix meets AA for normal text and AAA where chips include important action state labels
Handoff package includes CSS token names, React prop contract proposal, and migration notes for legacy pill components
Design review signoff from Console PM and Accessibility reviewer
design_notes: Chips represent lightweight annotations (status, estimate, region, promo) and must be visually distinct from primary badges and filter pills
Token-first approach: map every visual attribute to a semantic token (chip-bg-*, chip-fg-*, chip-border-*, chip-radius-*, chip-padding-*)
Spacing: use 4px grid with tokenized horizontal/vertical padding. Compact uses 4/6, regular 6/8, spacious 8/12
Iconography: chips may include 12px icons only; reserve larger icons for action buttons to avoid density clash
Interaction: chips support hover, pressed, focus-visible states. Focus-visible should be a 2px outline token (chip-focus-outline) separate from border color
Variant rules: primary (solid bg), subtle (transparent bg + border), inverse (for dark surface), ghost (text only)
decisions: Chips will be semantic (status|context|meta) rather than tied to use-case names to increase reusability
Use semantic tokens instead of direct color references to enable runtime theme switching and upcoming quantized palettes
Default chip height will target 24px for compact, 32px for regular, 40px for spacious to align with console density tokens
Avoid adding animations beyond subtle opacity changes; motion increases perceived CPU work in dense views
